title: Graphing a Stretched and Shifted Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = 2 / x^2 + 1 by starting with the standard graph y = 1 / x^2 and applying appropriate transformations.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = \frac{1}{x^2} \text{ stretched vertically by } 2 \text{ and shifted up } 1;\quad \text{VA: } x = 0,\quad \text{HA: } y = 1,\quad \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 0) \cup (0, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } (1, \infty)

steps.title: Identify the Vertical Stretch and Shift from y = 1/x^2
steps.explanation: Start with y = 1/x^2, stretch it vertically by a factor of 2 to get y = 2/x^2, and shift it upward by 1 unit to get y = 2/x^2 + 1.
steps.why: Multiplying by 2 stretches vertically by a factor of 2, and adding 1 shifts upward by 1.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote is x = 0 and the horizontal asymptote is y = 1. Since 2/x^2 > 0 for all x != 0, the range is (1, infinity).
steps.why: Adding 1 to positive values (0, infinity) produces the range (1, infinity).

steps.title: Analyze Symmetry and Guide Points
steps.explanation: The graph is symmetric about the y-axis with no x- or y-intercepts, passing through (+/-1, 3) and (+/-2, 3/2) and approaching y = 1 as x -> +/-infinity.
steps.why: Replacing x with -x leaves x^2 unchanged, confirming y-axis symmetry.
